runs.text: I'm always weirded out by this.
Where I live, they put some sort of pole with flaps hanging from it.
The flaps are perfectly positioned just slightly below to the height of bridges, etc. They are also somewhat heavy, but designed with the intention of not causing damage to the vehicles.
So if a vehicle is higher than the bridge, it firsts hits the flaps, making a heavy noise without damaging the vehicle, likely making the driver to stop before disaster.
Such a simple and relatively cheap solution. Why hasn't it been implemented here?
